knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem: The curve has equation $3 x^{2} + y^{2}=49$. The **tangent** line at $\left(4,-1\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
6 x+\left(2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(6 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{6 x}{2 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{24}{-2}=12
$$

The tangent line uses $m=12$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=12\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=12\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=12\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-1\right) \\
x-\left(4\right)&=-\frac{-1}{12} \\
x&=\frac{49}{12}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(\frac{49}{12},0\right)$.

question.:question/problem: The curve has equation $2 x^{2} + 3 y^{2}=45$. The **tangent** line at $\left(3,3\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 x+\left(6 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(6 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(4 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{4 x}{6 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{12}{18}=- \frac{2}{3}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=- \frac{2}{3}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(3\right)&=- \frac{2}{3}\left(x-\left(3\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{2}{3}\left(x-\left(3\right)\right)+\left(3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{2}{3}\left(0-\left(3\right)\right)+\left(3\right) \\
y&=5
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,5\right)$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem: The curve has equation $3 x^{2} + 4 y^{2}=63$. The **tangent** line at $\left(3,-3\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
6 x+\left(8 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(8 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(6 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{6 x}{8 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{18}{-24}=\frac{3}{4}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=\frac{3}{4}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-3\right)&=\frac{3}{4}\left(x-\left(3\right)\right) \\
y&=\frac{3}{4}\left(x-\left(3\right)\right)+\left(-3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{3}{4}\left(x-\left(3\right)\right)+\left(-3\right) \\
x-\left(3\right)&=-\frac{-3}{\frac{3}{4}} \\
x&=7
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(7,0\right)$.
